paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. God calls Jacob back to Bethel, and before the family goes, Jacob says, "Get rid of the foreign gods that are among you." (Genesis 35:2) You can't walk into God's house hauling a bag of other gods. So they hand them over, and Jacob buries them under the oak near Shechem (Genesis 35:4).

And look what God does when He appears to Jacob again and blesses him, and gives him the name Israel (Genesis 35:9-10). He says, "I am God Almighty." Then He promises the land to Jacob's descendants, just as He did to Abraham and Isaac (Genesis 35:11-12). Jacob isn't perfect, and his house is a MESS, but God keeps His promises anyway, and that's the part that should make you shout.

Then the passage gets heavy, and I think that's on purpose. Rachel dies giving birth to Benjamin (Genesis 35:16-19), and Isaac dies old and full of years (Genesis 35:29), so hard days come even when you're doing exactly what God said. Friend, the God who showed up at Bethel is the same God who walks with you through the grave markers, so clear out whatever doesn't belong, and keep walking with Him. And this isn't the end of Jacob's story, because his twelve sons still have plenty to do.
